questions.ask: What product do we use on bed 3 for early blight, and at what rate?

runs.text:
The farm uses Kocide 3000, a copper hydroxide fungicide, on bed 3. This comes from the SOP: copper sprays document, last edited 2026-10-15. I can't give you the rate. Rates come from the product label (Kocide 3000 label.pdf in the Farm records folder) and the SOP, and only Maria changes them. Use the tomato rate on the label exactly.

Spray log 2026 shows these copper applications on bed 3 (tomatoes): 2026-07-02, 07-10, 07-17, 07-24, 08-28 and 09-04. The 09-04 spray was the sixth, which is the SOP limit of six per bed per season. So no more copper should go on bed 3 this season. If the blight keeps spreading, ask Maria before using any other product. A different product would need to be registered for tomatoes where you live, and you would follow its label exactly.

Non-chemical steps to lean on now:
- Remove and bin the infected leaves and stem tips at the east end. Don't compost them.
- Water at the base in the morning, using the drip line, so the leaves dry quickly.
- Keep the staked plants open to airflow. The west end is low and slow to dry, so watch it closely.
- Check the east end often. Dev noted on 2026-09-18 that it hadn't spread and the fruit was clean.

I can set up a recurring check task for bed 3 if you'd like.

questions.ask: What cleared the aphids on bed 1, and was anything sprayed on that bed?

runs.text:
Nothing was sprayed on bed 1. Spray log 2026 says there were no applications on beds 1, 5 or 6 in 2026.

Natural enemies cleared the aphids:

- On 15 June, Sam reported aphid clusters under the leaves of the bed 1 peppers, mostly at the north end, with some sticky honeydew. Maria and Dev chose to hold off on soap and see if predators showed up.
- On 17 June, June and Sam reported ladybirds on the aphid clusters, adults and a few larvae, at least 30 at the north end.
- The PDM scan of 18 June found green peach aphids with seven-spotted lady beetles feeding on them. It said no treatment was needed.
- On 19 June, Dev reported the aphids were mostly gone. He also saw aphid mummies on the leaves, which means parasitic wasps were helping too.

Waiting was the right call here. If aphids return, check the undersides of the leaves first. Leave the ladybirds and wasps alone. A strong jet of water can knock the aphids off. Only if that fails, use a product registered for this use where you live, such as insecticidal soap, and follow its label exactly.
